SS4TKGT8.markdown:
[Uncategorized](https://doorbraak.be/onderwerp/zonder-categorie)

[ Forum ](https://doorbraak.be/forum)

# Artificial intelligence: no reason to panic

There are plenty of doomsday scenarios regarding the development of AI. Prof. Tijl De Bie urges calm.

—

Tijl De Bie is a data scientist and a full professor at Ghent University.

**MediaNation, the struggling company behind Business AM, ****will henceforth use Artificial Intelligence (AI)**** to write articles. That works perfectly well. The vast majority of newspaper articles written by humans, often under great time pressure, already lack much color or depth.**

Sometimes I also wonder how many magic mushrooms the journalist in question has consumed. Fact-checking is, after all, primarily there to give you a dressing down, dear social media users, not as part of journalistic practice. And for this opinion piece, I might well have gotten away with [this text](https://chat.openai.com/share/9b71e544-646f-42c5-acd5-2079886ca692) , written by ChatGPT, upon simple request with this prompt:

*“MediaNation, a media company that publishes the online news medium 'Business AM', is saving money by firing most of its journalists and replacing them with ChatGPT for translation and article writing. Can you write an opinion piece of approximately 500 words that starts with this anecdote and discusses what the impact of generative AI will be on white-collar workers?”*

Admittedly, [the result](https://chat.openai.com/share/9b71e544-646f-42c5-acd5-2079886ca692) is dry and stereotypical. But would it really stand out from the rest in some (other) daily or weekly papers?

## Existential fears

Quite a few scholarly analyses of generative AI systems (such as [ChatGPT](https://chat.openai.com/) ) extensively point out the shortcomings. The result is said to be soulless, devoid of any spark or sparkle. Worse still, they can 'hallucinate': in a sort of *stream of consciousness* , they spew out words that seem to make sense at first glance, but cannot be trusted one bit. They have no (self-)awareness, and 'empathy' is a word to ChatGPT like 'hemorrhoid' or 'kitchen table'.

That is all true, of course, and those shortcomings are inherent to current technology. But how long will it be before the next breakthrough addresses these flaws? And as I said: doesn't that same criticism often apply to human authors as well? Such skeptical views therefore seem primarily intended to soothe a kind of existential fear: surely we aren't losing our status as the smartest and most creative beings on this planet? The horror!

## White-collar workers

If you want to reap the benefits of generative AI and limit its risks, you had better put that fear aside. Although we are not there yet, it is safe to assume that sooner or later AI will grossly surpass humans in every intellectual task: stylistically and in terms of content, but also regarding creativity, (self-)awareness, and empathy – at least in the eyes of human observers. That offers enormous opportunities. Why, then, the anxiety?

Perhaps because AI, more than previous industrial revolutions, will affect the lives and work of white-collar workers and the intelligentsia: lawyers and notaries, bankers and insurers, accountants and HR professionals, doctors and researchers, designers and programmers, authors and journalists. The AI startups targeting these demographics are springing up like mushrooms.

Those who use their products will undoubtedly become more productive, while those who do not will fail competitively. Humans still remain the final decision-makers, but AI will help to sift through large amounts of data, find unexpected connections, make creative suggestions, write documents and reports, program large parts of computer software, and much more. The analogy with the *personal computer* is never far away: those who missed that boat are struggling today. The AI revolution promises to be more far-reaching, and faster.

## A bright future?

That realization creates tension and uncertainty, like a child on the eve of their first day of school. The challenge will be to steer the transition in the right direction. Many will need to retrain or upskill, and some will have to look for a new job. But if we succeed in this as a society, a future awaits us with greater prosperity, more free time, and a more fulfilling life.

However. Over the past quarter century, a period of intensive automation in knowledge sectors, the average number of [working hours](https://www.vlaanderen.be/statistiek-vlaanderen/arbeid/uren-beroepsarbeid-per-week) for the working population in Flanders has remained constant, while the [employment rate](https://www.vlaanderen.be/statistiek-vlaanderen/arbeid/werkzaamheidsgraad) rose. Although aging undoubtedly plays a role, anthropologist David Graeber also observes an increase in so-called *bullshit jobs* : jobs that are essentially useless to society, but which we perform out of a sort of puritanical-capitalist work ethic. They do not make you happy. More free time and satisfaction do not automatically follow from higher productivity.

Moreover, in order to be productive, the need for human contact will continue to diminish. Even in the healthcare sector, AI is gaining increasing traction, such as the [PARO seal](https://www.parorobots.com/) that offers comfort to those suffering from dementia. What will healthcare providers do with the time freed up? And will we derive the same satisfaction from professional and social contact with intelligent robots and chatbots, if they are behaviorally indistinguishable from humans (or animals), or are even superior to them by objective standards?

## Imagination

The real AI risk is therefore not an economic crisis, but rather a crisis of meaning.

["Only imagination can save us](https://www.lannoo.be/nl/alleen-verbeelding-kan-ons-redden) ," Michael De Cock titled his scintillating eulogy to the arts. He said it somewhat ironically, but his words could be more prophetic than many think. Imagination and connection.

A bumpy dinner service, hand-thrown by that good friend, has more value than an impeccable set from Ikea. A performance by your ten-year-old daughter or son surpasses a concert by, say, a laureate of the Queen Elisabeth Competition or Pommelien Thijs. A Van Gogh exposed as a forgery suddenly loses all its value. The dinner service is the friendship, the music is the parent-child bond, the painting is the painter himself. Similarly, an article written by a flesh-and-blood journalist with their own story will likely touch you more deeply than a flawless exposition by the next version of ChatGPT. Value lies in imagination and connection, not in the product itself—no matter how flawless it is.

## Long live AI, long live human imperfection

Therefore, parallel to the rise of AI, we could witness a revaluation of imperfection: the artisanal, the slow, the crooked, the authentic, the human.

I dare to quietly hope so, at least.

8JIHB2ML.title: Головна редакторка сайту 24 каналу Анастасія Зазуляк звільнилася разом з заступниками [AUTO-TRANSLATED IN ARC]
8JIHB2ML.markdown:
# The editor-in-chief of the Channel 24 website, Anastasia Zazulyak, resigned along with her deputies.

The editor-in-chief of the 24 Channel website, **Anastasia Zazulyak** , and her deputies , **Natalia Bodnar** , **Veronika Gavrylenko** , and **Emal Nabi,** decided to stop cooperating with the media due to a different vision of the future strategy with the holding's management. Anastasia Zazulyak reported this in a comment to "Media Detector".

*"Due to a different vision of the process with the holding's management and a different vision of the strategy of the future project, my team of deputies and I decided to end cooperation with the Channel 24 website. However, we believe that the site will have good management ahead and new innovative solutions will bring really cool results,"* the journalist said. 

According to Zazulyak, she and her team will continue to work on important social projects. They will be able to share details later. *“At the same time, we are open to new possible collaborations and will be happy to consider proposals* ,” the journalist added. 

According to a source from "Detector Media", the decision of the site's editors could be related to the management's intention to launch a news feed that will be created by artificial intelligence and reduce the number of journalists.

When asked by "DM" whether the holding's management really planned to lay off employees, Anastasia Zazulyak replied that no people had been laid off as of now, and she was not aware of further decisions by the management.

At the same time, she noted that AI tools are indeed "actively being implemented for the editorial team in some news creation processes."

*"My deputies and I, together with the development team, created tools that should help the editor in his work. We have no illusions about the future with AI tools. AI is an important factor in today's realities, and it is absolutely normal to implement tools, but the editorial office does not end there. Despite this, the value of people will always be higher than any machines, live texts will always have an advantage. And any tools need time for their high-quality implementation,"* said Anastasia Zazulyak.

Natalia Bodnar, Veronika Gavrylenko, and Emal Nabi, when asked by "DM" for comment, responded that Anastasia had already formulated their collective position regarding the decision to terminate cooperation with Channel 24.

*“We went through everything and survived thanks to wonderful people — the most valuable and important capital of the holding. Now our visions of how to develop this capital are different. When the current carries you onto the rocks, you need to gather all your strength and go ashore,” *[Veronika Gavrylenko wrote](https://www.facebook.com/nika.havrylenko/posts/pfbid02hgGsZBTCMUSvFx6FzDUrMqEr7Hgy836beqaPWzCo9JeBqteWCA6nCdYKGFiTUuvcl?locale=ru_RU) on her Facebook page.

*"I often say, if you want to change something for the better, start with yourself. If you want to help the country, people, start with yourself. And I tried to do that. And I didn't betray myself before, and I'm doing it now. That's why I'm leaving on the 24th. And although in reality, I planned to leave temporarily for an indefinite period, I'm leaving permanently. And I'm leaving with the best team. Because my values and our view on the development of the site no longer coincide with the company's management,"* Natalia Bodnar also [noted](https://www.facebook.com/natalya.bodnar.7/posts/pfbid0fsenJFKGQV54KWh2oertGJc1GryWnCRqSo6FwP36GUD5PsKLVu8cuMLE349y8q9wl) on Facebook.

*"I'm not a journalist by profession and probably didn't become one until the end, even by vocation. But having found myself in this unknown sphere 10 years ago by chance, I stayed here for a long time. Thanks to and for the sake of the people around me.*

*I don't believe in the story that people can be turned into just buttons for AI and service for instant chatbots. I love texts that are written at 2 am or 5 am, and these texts will never be replaced by a machine. I love to be amazed by human errors, because all this is present in each of us and without errors the world does not become worse or better, but for now it belongs to people. "The main value is people" is not just a corporate slogan for me, which politicians or heads of various companies love,"* Emal Nabi [shared](https://www.facebook.com/nabiemal/posts/pfbid026yXpU1gpW37MhEjWW2viijKSvbkmNabmTMoJLSrqfPyUJNNyqLpueYr1MHpynYo7l?locale=ru_RU) on his Facebook page.

**"Detector Media" also asked Roman Andreyk,** CEO of TRK "Lux" , why the team of editors of the site decided to leave. He replied that he would not disclose the reasons out of respect for the team. According to him, "it was an assessment of the work we did after lengthy discussions."

*"I appreciate everything the team did. Nastya Zazulyak personally, her deputies. I am sure that they did everything in such a way that it was the best of what was available. They did not pretend to do what they were doing, but they did, they tried. Another issue is that not everything works out. That's how it happens. This is life,"* said Andreyko.

When asked by "DM" whether this decision was related to the introduction of artificial intelligence into the work of the editorial office, Andreyko denied it.

*"AI has been working in our editorial office for a long time. And firing someone because of AI would sound too scandalous. Maybe even profitable, because it would immediately gain a lot of publicity. But no, that's not the case* ," said the CEO of TRK "Lux".

He also claims that information about the intention to reduce the number of journalists and replace them with artificial intelligence is not true.

Roman Andreyko will soon announce who will head the Channel 24 website.

**Read also:**

- [Anastasia Zazulyak, Channel 24: We believe in "healthy clickbait" — it has nothing to do with deception](https://detector.media/production/article/242964/2025-07-27-anastasiya-zazulyak-24-kanal-my-virymo-v-zdorovyy-klikbeyt-vin-ne-maie-nichogo-spilnogo-z-obmanom/)
- [How Channel 24 delivers news with AI and develops digital projects: Denis Zelenov in the "Media" podcast](https://detector.media/mediumy/article/235693/2024-12-08-yak-24-kanal-ozvuchuie-novyny-za-dopomogoyu-shi-ta-rozvyvaie-dydzhytal-proiekty-denys-zelenov-u-podkasti-mediumy/)

As a reminder, Anastasia Zazulyak has worked on the Channel 24 website since 2018. From 2022 to 2025, she was the host of morning broadcasts, hosted an international press review program, as well as weekly reviews of the week's top events on the channel's YouTube channel.

Since August 2022, [she has been the editor-in-chief of the website](https://detector.media/infospace/article/201573/2022-08-03-golovnoyu-redaktorkoyu-saytu-kanalu-24-stala-anastasiya-zazulyak/) , and was also responsible for the broadcaster's team of investigative journalists and the relevant direction. 

Natalia Bodnar has worked on the 24 Channel website since 2017. In recent years, she has been the deputy editor-in-chief and was responsible for content, SEO news, materials and interviews on military and social topics. She is the author of social and cultural projects "The Price of a Peaceful Sky", "Barricades of Dignity", "Famine and Moro: Memory of Generations", "Ukrainian Christmas" and co-author of the project "SVOI".

Emal Nabi was the editor-in-chief of the news publication iPress.ua from 2017 to 2019. Since 2019, he has joined the team of Channel 24, where he was responsible for the geopolitics and international analytics department. He has published scientific articles on the topic of international order and the Middle East in scientific collections and almanacs.

Veronika Gavrylenko worked as a journalist for the website "Chernivetskyi Promin", a website editor and SMM editor at the Media Growth Agency "ABO". In 2019, she joined Channel 24, and since 2022 she has been the deputy editor-in-chief, responsible for the technical and SEO areas of the website.
